entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts claim zero-free half-planes for zeta. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that every finite-order Hecke L-function over Q(√-3) and every Dirichlet L-function, zeta included, has no zero with Re s > 7/8, with the principal pole at s=1 allowed. Its Part I proves the same statement with 11/12 in place of 7/8 (Theorem 'The 11/12 half-plane'), and Part II builds on that. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims the weaker half-plane Re s > 11/12 for the same families, by a route through a mean-square bound for twisted Möbius sums; it describes the 7/8 result as stronger. For zeta, the claim is that every nontrivial zero has real part at most 7/8 (Sept 30) or at most 11/12 (Oct 5).
entries.delivers: A fixed zero-free strip next to the line Re s = 1 for zeta: no nontrivial zero with real part in (7/8, 1) according to Sept 30, or in (11/12, 1) according to Oct 5. Zeros with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12) are not restricted to any line, so the location question is not decided. The Sept 30 introduction says that the theorem does not establish the Riemann hypothesis or its generalized versions.
entries.remains: That every nontrivial zero of zeta with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12) has real part exactly 1/2. The list's universal claim is otherwise untouched.
entries.direction: proves a zero-free half-plane (partial result toward RH, the quasi-RH)
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis is stated. Some steps are taken from published work without proof here: the number-field quadratic large sieve of Goldmakher and Louvel, the cubic theta coefficient and transformation formulas of Patterson and Dunn–Radziwiłł, Heath-Brown's admissible-exponent method, and the Hecke functional equation. Sept 30's Part II depends on its own Part I, which it uses to get β* ≤ 11/12 and hence Δ ≤ 1/24. Oct 5 does not depend on Sept 30; its introduction cites Sept 30 only for the stronger 7/8 result.
entries.doubts: (1) The Sept 30 TeX is about 16,700 lines. I read the statements, the proof overview, the Part I/II transition, the final assembly and a few lemma statements, not the body. The argument is a contradiction (assume β* > 7/8) that depends on many declared hypotheses, some of which the text says are 'verified' later. Near line 5648 the text calls the high identity 'a hypothesis to be proved for the physical expression, not its definition'; I did not trace where that is discharged. (2) Oct 5 calls its outline a sketch that suppresses coprimality conditions, local factors and smoothing; the full argument is in later sections. I read the reduction and the proof of Proposition thm:ms, which reduces to Proposition 'canonical' and the iteration, but not the reflection, transfer or appendix sections. (3) The Oct 5 README says 'This paper was written with human assistance.' The Sept 30 and Oct 1 READMEs say no such thing.

entries.what_happened: The same two zero-free-region manuscripts. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that every Dirichlet L-function, zeta included, has no zero with Re s > 7/8. It gets there from finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√-3), using the factorisation of the norm-composed character into L(s,χ)L(s,χχ_{-3}) up to finitely many Euler factors that are nonzero for Re s > 0 (Proposition 'Quadratic transfer'). 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims the same families have no zeros with Re s > 11/12, stating the factorisation explicitly. Neither manuscript says anything about the critical line.
entries.delivers: For every Dirichlet L-function (all moduli and characters, the principal one included with its pole at s=1 allowed), no nontrivial zero with Re s > 7/8 (Sept 30) or Re s > 11/12 (Oct 5). This is a zero-free half-plane, not GRH: zeros with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 are not located on Re s = 1/2 or anywhere else.
entries.remains: Every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet L-function with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12), and the claim that each such zero has real part exactly 1/2.
entries.direction: proves a zero-free half-plane for all Dirichlet L-functions (partial result toward GRH)
entries.conditional_on: As in riemann-hypothesis: no unproven hypothesis is stated, and published results are used as black boxes for some steps. The Dirichlet claim is derived inside each manuscript from its Hecke claim, which is proved in the same manuscript. Oct 5 does not depend on Sept 30.
entries.doubts: The proof-level caveats in riemann-hypothesis apply. The Dirichlet statement is a short transfer from the Hecke statement; Sept 30's proof of it is a few lines, and it relies on the Euler factors omitted from the transfer being nonzero in Re s > 0, which the text asserts. The Sept 30 introduction states that the theorem does not establish the generalized Riemann hypothesis.

entries.what_happened: The two zero-free-region manuscripts treat only finite-order Hecke characters of F = Q(√-3), that is, Hecke characters of trivial infinite type (GL(1) over F), together with the Dirichlet L-functions obtained from them by the transfer (GL(1) over Q). 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that these have no zeros with Re s > 7/8; 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims no zeros with Re s > 11/12. The manuscripts do not treat infinite-type Hecke characters, GL(n) for n ≥ 2, or any other automorphic L-functions.
entries.delivers: Zero-free half-planes (Re s > 7/8 by Sept 30, Re s > 11/12 by Oct 5) for finite-order Hecke L-functions of Q(√-3) and for all Dirichlet L-functions. Nothing for other automorphic L-functions, and nothing on the location of zeros with Re s ≤ 7/8, so the bullet's claim is not decided.
entries.remains: All other automorphic L-functions (GL(n) for n ≥ 2, infinite-type Hecke L-functions over any number field, and so on), and the location claim Re ρ = 1/2 for every nontrivial zero of every automorphic L-function.
entries.direction: proves a zero-free half-plane for a restricted class of automorphic L-functions (partial result toward grand RH)
entries.conditional_on: As in riemann-hypothesis: no unproven hypothesis is stated, and published results are used as black boxes for some steps. Oct 5 does not depend on Sept 30.
entries.doubts: The proof-level caveats in riemann-hypothesis apply. The Sept 30 introduction says that the theorem does not establish the generalized versions of the Riemann hypothesis.

entries.what_happened: 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros' (Oct 1 2026) claims an absolute c > 0 such that every real zero β in (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3 satisfies (1−β) log q ≥ c. So no such zero lies in (1 − c/log q, 1). The paper calls this its logarithmic formulation of the Landau–Siegel zero problem. The proof is a contradiction argument: a sequence of real zeros with (1−β) log q → 0 is assumed; a prime-bias bound from the logarithmic derivative of the Hadamard product forces primes with χ(p) = −1 to carry logarithmic mass; an interpolation determinant in the biquadratic field Q(√d, √2) is divisible by many primes through the Frobenius relation, but its norm is bounded above; the comparison gives 1 ≤ 7/8. Two zero-free-half-plane manuscripts also bear on the question. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) says its theorem 'rules out the existence of Landau–Siegel zeros', and it excludes real zeros of all Dirichlet L-functions in (11/12, 1). 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) excludes them in (7/8, 1). Either fixed-window claim, if correct, gives the log-scale exclusion with δ = (log 3)/8, since |D| ≥ 3 for nonprincipal real characters.
entries.delivers: For fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 (primitive nonprincipal real characters χ_D of conductor q = |D| ≥ 3) there is one absolute δ > 0, namely δ = c with c not computed, such that L(σ, χ_D) has no zero for 1 − δ/log|D| < σ < 1. So the 'is there δ > 0' form has answer yes, and the claim is that Siegel zeros, defined by this log-scale window, do not exist. The frozen wording does not define 'Siegel zero', and the paper's own statement is the log-scale one; the match depends on that definition. The text does not claim the frozen wording as literally stated.
entries.remains: Under the Oct 1 theorem alone: real zeros at distance at least c/log q from 1, which it does not exclude; the value of c; non-real characters; and the trivial character D = 1 (ζ), which is outside the theorem. Under the fixed-window claims, the real zeros in (0, 7/8] (Sept 30) or (0, 11/12] (Oct 5).
entries.direction: proves uniform exclusion of Siegel zeros on the log scale (no real zeros in the window 1 − c/log q < β < 1); the zero-free half-plane claims give a stronger fixed-window exclusion
entries.conditional_on: Oct 1 assumes no hypothesis and cites no other manuscript. It uses standard analytic facts (the Hadamard product and functional equation, Mertens and Chebyshev bounds, Euler's criterion, the Frobenius map in a number field). Siegel's, Page's and Deuring–Heilbronn's results are cited as background. The Sept 30 and Oct 5 implications rest on those manuscripts' own proofs and the literature listed in riemann-hypothesis.
entries.doubts: (1) The constant c is not computed. The argument is a contradiction, so c is not effective, and the text does not say this in so many words. (2) The step that handles the finitely many small conductors is one sentence: 'for each of them L(1,χ) ≠ 0 ... analyticity therefore prevents zeros from accumulating at 1'. (3) The field d = 2 (conductor 8) is excluded 'temporarily' and dealt with by passing to q → ∞. (4) The paper says it proves only the logarithmic formulation, so the frozen question is not restated verbatim. (5) The Oct 5 README says 'This paper was written with human assistance.' The Oct 1 README says nothing of the kind.

entries.what_happened: No zero-density estimate is proved. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that no zero of zeta, and no zero of any Dirichlet L-function, has real part above 7/8. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims the same with 11/12. The Sept 30 introduction mentions zero-density bounds (Guth and Maynard) only as background and says they answer a different question.
entries.delivers: For σ in (7/8, 1] the zero count N(σ,T) is zero for every T according to Sept 30, so the displayed bound N(σ,T) ≪ T^(2(1−σ)+ε) holds trivially there; according to Oct 5, the same holds for σ in (11/12, 1]. This is the vacuous end of the range, not a density estimate. Nothing is claimed for 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12), and no exponent is obtained or compared.
entries.remains: The range 1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12) for zeta, where the zero count and the exponent 2(1−σ)+ε are untouched; uniformity in T; and the ε-loss question.
entries.direction: makes the density bound vacuous above 7/8 (or 11/12), via a zero-free region; proves no zero-density estimate
entries.conditional_on: The vacuous range rests entirely on the zero-free claims in the two manuscripts, with the conditions listed in riemann-hypothesis.
entries.doubts: The vacuous range is only as secure as the zero-free claims in riemann-hypothesis. Nothing else specific to this bullet.

entries.not_relevant_because: None of the three manuscripts says anything about ζ(1/2+it) as t → ∞. The zero-free half-planes (Re s > 7/8 in 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8'; Re s > 11/12 in 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis') lie strictly to the right of the critical line and give no growth bound there. The only growth estimate on the critical line in the family is a crude Hecke strip bound, |L(σ+it,ψ)| ≪ Q^(3/5)(3+|t|)^2 for −1/10 ≤ σ ≤ 11/10 (Sept 30, Lemma 'Hecke strip growth'), used as an internal technical input; its t^2 exponent is far from the o(t^ε) claim.
